question: Explain overfitting, compare L2 regularization and early stopping, then summarize their advantages.
answer: L2 regularization, also known as weight decay, penalizes the sum of squared weights, shrinking them towards zero without setting them exactly to zero. [S1] This method is smooth and works well with gradient-based optimizers, keeping all features. [S6] However, early stopping requires a held-out validation set, is sensitive to the patience value, and noisy validation curves can trigger a premature stop. [S1] Both methods are often combined, with early stopping being the cheaper and more reproducible option [S1] [S6] [S7].

citations.text:
L2 regularization and early stopping
3. Early stopping Early stopping monitors validation loss during training and stops when it has not
improved for a fixed number of epochs (the patience); the best checkpoint is restored. Advantages:
it needs no change to the model, saves training compute, and the stopping epoch acts as an
implicit regularizer. Disadvantages: it requires a held-out validation set that is then not used for
training, results are sensitive to the patience value, and noisy validation curves can trigger a
premature stop. 4. Dropout Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction p of hidden units at each training
step so units cannot co-adapt. It is applied only during training. It is mainly used for neural
networks.

citations.title: Ml Overfitting Mitigation Guide
citations.text:
Dropout and choosing between methods
5. Choosing between methods L2 and early stopping are complementary and are often combined.
Early stopping is cheapest; L2 gives a smoother, more reproducible solution. Compare methods by
validation accuracy, never by training accuracy.

Ways to reduce overfitting include collecting more training data, simplifying the model, regularization (L1 and L2 penalties that shrink weights; L1 can drive weights to exactly zero), early stopping, dropout for neural networks, feature selection and cross-validation to choose hyperparameters. Learning curves, which plot error against training set size, help diagnose whether a model suffers from high bias or high variance.

S5.text:
3. Regularization Strength in scikit-learn
In scikit-learn LogisticRegression the parameter C is the inverse of the regularization strength: a
smaller C means stronger regularization, and the default is C=1.0. For Ridge regression the
parameter alpha works the opposite way: a larger alpha means stronger shrinkage.
L2 regularization (ridge) shrinks all weights toward zero; L1 regularization (lasso) can set some
weights exactly to zero and therefore performs feature selection.
